<style>
.zg-locked{display:none !important}
.zg-gate.zg-done{display:none !important}
.zg-reveal{animation:zgFadeIn .6s ease both}
@keyframes zgFadeIn{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(14px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}
.zg-fade{position:relative;height:120px;margin-bottom:-40px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(244,249,255,0) 0%,#F4F9FF 82%);pointer-events:none}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.zg-reveal{animation:none}}
</style>
<script>
(function(){
  function reveal(){
    var loc=document.querySelectorAll('.zg-locked');
    for(var i=0;i<loc.length;i++){loc[i].classList.add('zg-reveal');loc[i].classList.remove('zg-locked');}
    var g=document.querySelectorAll('.zg-gate');for(var j=0;j<g.length;j++){g[j].classList.add('zg-done');}
    var fd=document.querySelectorAll('.zg-fade');for(var m=0;m<fd.length;m++){fd[m].style.display='none';}
    var t=document.querySelector('.zg-reveal');if(t){setTimeout(function(){t.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth',block:'start'});},260);}
  }
  window.zgReveal=reveal;
  // Production (Elementor Pro Forms): reveal only after a validated, captured submission.
  if(window.jQuery){window.jQuery(document).on('submit_success',reveal);}
  // Fallback for the gallery preview / non-Pro sites: reveal when the gate button is used.
  function bindFallback(){
    var pro=!!(window.elementorProFrontend||(window.elementorFrontend&&window.elementorFrontend.config));
    if(pro)return;
    var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.zg-gate button, .zg-gate [type=submit]');
    for(var i=0;i<btns.length;i++){btns[i].addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();reveal();});}
    var forms=document.querySelectorAll('.zg-gate form');
    for(var k=0;k<forms.length;k++){forms[k].addEventListener('submit',function(e){e.preventDefault();reveal();});}
  }
  if(document.readyState!=='loading')bindFallback();else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',bindFallback);
})();
</script>

This report summarises findings from the India HR Pulse 2026 survey, a community initiative by Zimyo Research to benchmark how HR and business leaders across India (and select GCC markets) are experiencing attrition, leadership, data maturity, and the changing shape of HR’s mandate.

Our exclusive HR Pulse survey ran across India and select GCC markets, with responses collected between 1 June and 6 August 2026. Every response was verified against a work email and company record, and analysed only in aggregate. Respondents span organisations from under 50 employees to enterprises of several thousand, across technology, manufacturing, retail, financial services, healthcare and professional services.

Inside the full report, each of the four headline metrics is broken down by company size, sector and region, alongside the practices that separate the top quartile from the rest — from how they retain people, to how ready they are for the new Labour Codes.

The chapters that follow move from the headline numbers into the detail: what is driving attrition, why most HR decisions are still made without structured data, where the talent funnel leaks, and how far organisations really are from Labour Code readiness. Each section pairs the survey data with a clear read on what the leading teams are doing differently, and what it would take to close the gap.

settings.editor: 59.3% of leaders name attrition & retention as their top concern. Here is where it bites hardest.
Across sizes and sectors, keeping people beat hiring, cost and compliance as the single biggest worry — and the pressure is highest in fast-scaling mid-market teams.

icon_list.text: Mid-market teams feel it most acutely
Notice-period exits cluster around appraisal cycles

settings.title: Most HR decisions run on gut, not data

settings.editor: 69.1% make HR decisions without structured employee data — the clearest gap the survey found.

settings.title: Decisions without a single source of truth

settings.editor: Employee data is still scattered across spreadsheets, email and disconnected tools, so most teams cannot answer basic questions about their own workforce without manual effort.

icon_list.text: Reporting is mostly manual and retrospective
Few teams can segment attrition in real time
One connected record is the strongest predictor of maturity

settings.editor: A 78.4% overall offer-to-join rate means roughly one in five accepted offers never starts.
Offer-to-join has slipped as candidates hold multiple offers. The leaders shorten time-to-offer and stay engaged through the notice period to protect the join rate.

icon_list.text: Drop-off peaks during long notice periods
Faster offers correlate with higher joins
Structured pre-boarding lifts the rate materially

settings.editor: 46.6% of organisations are not yet ready for the new Labour Codes. Readiness drops sharply with complexity.
The gap: readiness falls the moment a business spans states or entities. Teams whose payroll applies state-wise rules automatically report far higher confidence than those tracking the codes by hand.

settings.title: Four moves that close the gap
Put people data on one record

settings.editor: Every downstream metric — attrition, funnel, readiness — depends on a single source of truth. The teams that consolidated first are the ones making decisions on data, not instinct.
Leaders track attrition by team, tenure and manager in real time, and run stay-interviews before the appraisal-cycle exits, not after.
Shorter time-to-offer and structured pre-boarding through the notice period are the two levers most correlated with higher joins in the data.
